subject: Request: methodology for credit apportionment during overlapping maintenance and third-party degradations
messages:
From: Sam Wilkes <sam.wilkes@orionlogistics.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Partial capacity during rolling maintenance — request for credit

Hi Redwood team,

We observed a partial degradation that impacted our production API traffic during your Nov 29 rolling maintenance window. Between 2026-11-29 12:56 UTC and 2026-11-29 13:38 UTC we saw increased median latency (+420ms), a spike in 5xx errors (~3.6% of calls), and degraded throughput for specific endpoints (text-generation/v1). Our ops team captured server-side traces and a sample request log — attaching the CSV export.

This period overlaps with the scheduled maintenance you published for 12:45–13:15 UTC. However, our traffic shows degradation that started ~11 minutes before your published start time and persisted ~23 minutes after the published end. Because of the overlap and different start/end times, we’d like clarification on how Redwood computes "available" minutes and whether we are eligible for an SLA credit for the observed partial degradation.

We are on the Dedicated plan under contract DL-2025-0098. Our finance lead has asked us to submit a formal credit request, so we need:
- The window(s) Redwood will consider for credit calculation (full maintenance, partial degraded minutes, excluded third-party outages).
- The formula you will apply to apportion credit when a maintenance window and a third-party outage overlap (e.g., would you subtract third-party downtime first?).
- A timeline for a decision (we need an answer before our invoice cycles on Dec 5).

Attached: orion_outage_log_20261129.csv

Thanks,
Sam Wilkes
SRE Lead — Orion Logistics

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Partial capacity during rolling maintenance — request for credit

Hi Sam — thanks for the detailed note and the CSV. I’ve opened this for review with our reliability and billing teams (cc: Marissa). Quick answers while we investigate:

1) We do perform a minute-granular availability calculation against the contract SLA metric (successful request rate per minute). When a minute is below the availability threshold, it’s counted as degraded.
2) Our standard approach is to apportion credit to the customer for minutes where Redwood is the primary cause. If a third-party provider is the root cause (e.g., an upstream CDN failure), we typically exclude those minutes per the service-dependency exclusion in section 4.2 of the SLA (attached excerpt).
3) When maintenance windows overlap with degradations, we evaluate two things: the published maintenance window and the observed event timings. If the observed degradation extends beyond the published maintenance, eligible minutes are the subset where Redwood’s serving tier was responsible.

To be concrete and transparent, could you confirm:
- Which request logs in your CSV are for the Dedicated cluster hostname (you have both hosted endpoints and a proxy)?
- Do you have any traces tying errors to our origin versus the upstream CDN?

We’ll run a minute-by-minute availability calculation and share the apportionment workbook (I’ll attach our internal calc). I expect a formal response no later than Wed, Dec 1.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Manager, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Partial capacity during rolling maintenance — request for credit

Forwarding Sam’s logs — they’re asking for how we apportion credits when maintenance and external CDN interruptions overlap. Attaching our apportionment worksheet.

Key points I think we need to decide quickly:
- Do we subtract third-party outage minutes first (i.e., exclude them entirely) and then compute degraded Redwood minutes, or do we compute the total degraded minutes and then deduct third-party contribution proportionally? Sam’s CSV shows a ~12-minute complete unreachability from ops@edgepartners.io at 13:05–13:17 UTC.
- The contract language (section 4.2) allows exclusion for dependencies, but it’s not explicit about overlapping maintenance windows. If we exclude third-party minutes first, the remaining degraded minutes attributable to Redwood are smaller and likely produce a token credit. If we apportion proportionally, the customer could receive a larger credit.

Marissa — your view? Rishi — if you can run the minute-by-minute metric on cluster dc-west-2-ded-4 and append the calculation to the workbook, that’ll help. I’m sensitive to the Dec 5 invoice cutoff.

Thanks,
Ava

Subject: Proposed apportionment and next steps — Orion Logistics (DL-2025-0098)

Hi Sam — thanks for your patience. We completed an internal review (attached workbook: redwood_apportionment_calc.xlsx) and I wanted to summarize our proposed approach so we can close this by Dec 3 ahead of your invoice.

Summary of findings
- Observed degradation window (customer logs): 2026-11-29 12:56–13:38 UTC
- Redwood Dedicated cluster impacted minutes (per our minute granular telemetry): 12:59–13:34 UTC (35 minutes below the SLA availability threshold)
- Upstream CDN impact (edgepartners.io): 13:05–13:17 UTC (12 minutes of reduced reachability from their side)

How we applied the apportionment methodology
1) We exclude full-minute failures that we can attribute exclusively to a third-party dependency (edgepartners.io) — i.e., 13:05–13:16 UTC (12 minutes). These are excluded in line with the service-dependency exclusion referenced in the SLA excerpt (attached).
2) For the remaining degraded minutes where our telemetry shows Redwood’s serving tier contributed (12:59–13:04 and 13:17–13:34 UTC), we calculate a pro-rated credit equal to the ratio of degraded minutes to total minutes in the billing period. For your November billing period that equates to a 0.92% credit on the monthly Dedicated invoice.

Why we chose exclusion-first
- The contract explicitly allows exclusion for third-party dependencies. Operationally, it reduces double-counting of incidents where the upstream is the primary root cause. It’s also consistent with precedent we have applied on similar dedicated plans.

Deliverables and next steps
- Attached workbook with minute-by-minute marks and formulas (redwood_apportionment_calc.xlsx).
- An excerpt of the SLA showing the dependency exclusion clause (sla-excerpt.pdf).
- If you accept the proposed credit (0.92% of the Nov invoice), reply to this message and I’ll route the credit through finance. If you prefer we run a proportional apportionment model instead, we can do that and provide the alternate calculation within 24 hours.

DocuSign for acceptance: https://docusign.redwood.ai/arc/DL-2025-0098/credit-acceptance

Please advise which option you prefer. If you accept the exclusion-first result, we’ll issue the credit before your Dec 5 invoice.

Best regards,
Ava Chen
